class.name: GameModeSettings
class.brief_description: Resource describing which game mode script, pawn and controller a level uses.
class.description: A [Level] may carry its own instance to override the project-wide default. The pawn scene must contain a [PawnHandler]: either as its root, or anywhere below it. The first one found in a recursive search is used. Without one the pawn still spawns but cannot be possessed, and the framework warns instead of failing.

method.name: get_pawn_scene_for_player
method.description: The entry in [member pawn_scene_overrides] for this player, or [member pawn_scene] when there is none.

members.member: When true, a button pressed on a device no player owns logs a new player in, up to [member max_local_players]. Filter which devices are allowed with [method GameMode._can_join].
Root must be a [GameState]. Left unset, a plain one is created. Use a scene rather than a script when you want to hang a [MultiplayerSpawner] or [MultiplayerSynchronizer] off it.

How many humans may share this machine. [b]Leaving it at 1 is what keeps a single player project unchanged[/b]: player 0 is created holding [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_ALL], so every device drives it exactly as the [Input] singleton always did. Raising it without narrowing player 0 to a specific device slot leaves nothing for anyone else, and the framework warns about that.
Indexed by player index, for games where player 2 is a different character. Falls back to [member pawn_scene] where the array is short or the entry is null.
Root must be a [PlayerState]. Left unset, a plain one is created.
